# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 23 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_023_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 4, Chapter 2

**1** Once past the beast, about thirty feet further down the road, a young woman appeared coming toward me. She looked like she was just stepping out of a wedding — dressed all in white, white sandals, a veil across her forehead, a white turban, and hair that was white as well. **2** I recognized her from earlier visions: the Church. My heart lifted with joy. She greeted me: "Hello, man of God!" "Hello, my lady!" I replied. **3** "Anything happen to you on the road?" she asked. "My lady, I encountered an enormous beast — something that could have destroyed whole populations. But by the power and mercy of God, I got through." **4** "Good that you got through," she said, "because you did exactly the right thing: you put your worry in God's hands and opened your heart to the Lord, trusting that there was no other way to be saved except through his great and glorious name. So the Lord sent his angel — the one who has authority over the beasts, Segri — and he shut the beast's mouth so it couldn't touch you. You passed through a great tribulation because of your faith and your refusal to doubt in the face of that terrifying thing. **5** Now go and tell God's chosen people what he has done. Tell them: this beast is a preview of the great tribulation that is coming. If you prepare yourselves now — if you repent wholeheartedly before the Lord — you will be able to get through it, as long as your hearts are clean and spotless and you serve the Lord faithfully for the rest of your lives. Dump your burdens on the Lord and he will carry them. **6** And you double-minded people — believe! Believe that God can do anything, that he can turn his anger aside from you. He sends suffering on those who refuse to trust him. Those who hear these words and still disobey — it would have been better for them to have never been born."

---

*PNEUMA note: "Dump your burdens on the Lord" is a vivid rendering of 1 Pet 5:7 / Psalm 55:22 — the Greek epirrhipto = cast/throw upon. The stark finality of the "better not born" echoes the Jesus tradition.*
